I personally used these videos to get myself started. After about a month, I was conversational enough to be able to Skype with Deaf ASL users effectively.
How different is ASL from say British Sign language. If you know one would you be able to communicate with someone who knows the other?

ASL and British Sign Language are completely different from each other. For example, their fingerspelling (hand alphabet) is different in that ASL uses one hand for all letters, and British uses two hands for all but one letter (C is spelled with one hand). Aside from that, signs are also fundamentally different with a number overlapping (like sorry), but others having completely different meanings.

My husband who is Deaf and from New Jersey and myself (only know ASL) actually have run into Deaf people in London, but communication was near impossible. There were some signs we would know of each other's sign language, but nowhere near enough to have a comprehensive conversation.

The difference of sign languages vs spoken languages I like to potray by saying Irish, British, American and Australian sign languages are all very different from each other and it's very difficult to understand users of those sign languages - even though the primary spoken language in those countries is English and fully understandable in all combinations (very, very heavy accents/dialects not included).

This is always either the first or the second question that comes up - is sign language universal?
